newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - mogas centre stage with $5 rise.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - mogas centre stage with $5 rise.

text.p: Gasoline swaps whipped higher on Friday gaining $5 or so, reaffirming its headline grabbing qualities.
Other oil product swaps were forced into the shadow after gasoline swaps jumped higher on news of a downed catalytic cracker at Shell's Pernis refinery.

Traders said an already tight supply situation in both NWE, the Mediterranean and most importantly the United States was exacerbated by news of the downed cracker which will be out of commission for three months, two of which will be planned maintenance.
Wet prices soared by $8 or so, but swaps were restricted to a $5 or so gain. Antwerp barrels sold at $212.00, $212.50 with Rotterdam storage selling at $213.50.
August swaps were around $210 from $205.50 with the backwardation into September extending because better supplies are anticipated in NWE around August 15-20.
The loss of 100,000 tonnes of gasoline a month from Pernis could change the complexion of the market, but so far most swaps dealers see the backwardation into September remaining.
Brent crude CFDs were a few cents firmer with August 4-8 pegged at +14 cents against September Brent from +10 cents with August 11-15 put at flat against -2/3 cents.
August 18-22 was assessed around -4/5 cents against September compared with Thursday's -6/7 cents and August 25-29 was put at -10 cents from -12 cents.
August 11-15 was understood to have traded at September +1 cent and a rol of August 11-15 versus 18-22 was done at +6 cents.

Heavy fuel was a touch stronger, but the market was very slow. Traders said August was put around $91.50-92.50 with the high/low spread narrowing. They said August low sulphur swaps had eased down to $93-94 with September in contango at $95-96.
Naphtha piggy-backed on gasoline's rise by putting on $1 to around $192 for August.
Gas oil crack spreads were seen at $4.55 with for both 4Q and 1Q.
